artist.name: Demo Artist
artist.tagline: Visual artist working with pattern and print
artist.statement:
This is placeholder text for the Raisonne demo. The demo artist is fictional: the name, the statement, the exhibitions and the on-chain records are made up so that a fresh install has something to show.

Replace this with your own statement in your content, or run the importer with your wallets to build the catalogue from what you minted.
artist.bio:
Demo Artist is a fictional artist used to demonstrate Raisonne, an open-source catalogue raisonne for on-chain artists. Their works on this demo site are public-domain decorative papers from The Metropolitan Museum of Art, shared under the Open Access (CC0) programme, standing in for artworks.

Every exhibition, award and press item listed here is invented, and every contract address is a placeholder that holds no tokens.

series.name: Paste Grounds
series.description: A fictional series for the Raisonne demo. Brushed and combed colour fields, each a single sheet, minted as unique tokens. The images are 18th-century paste papers from The Met, shared under CC0.

story.title: About this series
story.body: Twenty-four sheets, each combed once and photographed once. The series began as a way of asking what a printed ground still carries when it is minted, and what it quietly loses.

children.text: Everything on this page is placeholder text for the Raisonne demo. The artist, the venues and the dates are invented; the images are public-domain works from The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
Paste paper is made by brushing coloured paste onto damp sheets and drawing a comb through it. Nothing can be corrected: the mark is the record of one pass of the hand.
A ground is not a background. It is the first decision.
